title: Code Coverage: Signal, Not a Guarantee

scenes.say: Does a high code coverage number mean your code is actually bug-free?

scenes.label: Coverage
scenes.sub: Shows what percent of your code runs during tests.
scenes.say: Code coverage tells you what percent of your code actually runs when you run your tests.

scenes.title: Coverage Report
scenes.say: You might see a report showing ninety five percent coverage. That looks great, but what does it really mean?
High coverage means most lines run during tests, but it doesn't catch missing edge cases or guarantee your tests actually check for the right results.

scenes.question: Is 100% coverage always enough?
scenes.wrong: Yes, it means all bugs are caught.
scenes.right: No, you can miss important checks even with full coverage.
scenes.say: Here's a classic trap: Is full coverage always enough? Not really. You can still miss important checks, even if every line runs.
